title: What is known about 1RB1LB_1RC0RD_0LA1RE_0RF1LC_1LA0RB_---1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LB_1RC0RD_0LA1RE_0RF1LC_1LA0RB_---1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Left of the start the tape is a block of 1011 words, which grows by one word every two rounds, then a binary counter (about three cells a bit), then junk: a run of 1110 words and a second, slower counter. Lean proves the left-end turns and the counter's two carries for all lengths, and that a counter of 2m digits counts through all 4m values (count). Each overflow of the counter eats one or two junk words; when the junk is used up the machine restarts: the whole block turns into junk and the counter into the new slow counter. The blank-tape run restarts at round 25,515,382 with 12,757,674 words of new junk. Jumping from overflow to overflow (checked against the machine at small sizes, extrapolated beyond) the next two epochs also end in restarts, not halts; the one after that starts with a junk length of about 217,010,257 words, and whether it halts depends on arithmetic properties of that number that are out of reach. Halting configurations do exist in the same family, so no closed family of configurations avoids them without that arithmetic.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 28,354 cells have been visited and 21,267 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The turns at the left end, for every block length
claims.text: From 0^inf 0 0 (1110)^(n+1) A> 1011 R the machine crosses the whole block leftwards (rewriting each word as it passes), bounces off the blank tape and crosses it back, reaching 0^inf 111 (0111)^(n+1) 111 E> R in 20n+38 steps; and from the record in B, 0^inf B> 0 10 (1011)^n R, it reaches 0^inf 111 (0111)^n 0 B> R in 8n+11 steps. For all n and every tape R.

claims.title: The block grows by one word every two rounds
claims.text: At the records in B the tape is 0^inf B> 0 10 (1011)^N J T with the junction J alternately 1010 1011 and 11 1011; N goes up by one every two rounds and the left end moves out by two cells a round. Checked for the first 24,522 rounds (3·109 steps).

claims.title: A reduced run, checked against the machine
claims.text: Since the block is crossed word by word, the part right of it does not depend on N. c/m3red.c keeps the block at 40 words; for the first 24,522 rounds its tape right of the block agrees with the full machine at every round.

claims.title: No halt before the first restart (round 25,515,382)
claims.text: The reduced run (c/m3red.c, block cut to 40 words) is faithful as long as the block is only crossed, which holds until the first restart at round 25,515,382 (about 3·1015 machine steps); up to there it shows no halt. The region right of the block widens by two cells only at the overflows of rounds 349,558, 8,738,166 and 25,515,382. Correction: an earlier version of this page claimed 108 rounds without a halt from the same run; past the restart the cut block makes the reduced run wrong (the real block becomes junk there), so only the rounds before it count.

claims.title: The part right of the block is a binary counter
claims.text: Counting, from one round to the next, how far into T the changes reach, 2,000,000 rounds give depths 12, 14, 18, 20, 24, 26, ... cells with 499,998, 250,000, 124,999, 62,499, 31,249, ... rounds: each depth half as often as the one before, about three cells a bit. This is the carry pattern of a binary counter that goes up by one every two rounds.

claims.title: The counter's carries, and a full count, for every width
claims.text: Write the counter with digit i as 1010/1111 (0/1) for even i and 10/11 for odd i, least significant first, right after the junction 1010 1011. Two rounds turn B> 0 10 (1011)^n 1010 1011 (111111)^m 1010 R into the same with (1011)^(n+1) and (101010)^m 1111 R (26m+40n+122 steps), and (111111)^m 1111 10 R into (101010)^m 1010 11 R (26m+40n+128 steps). By induction on m, a counter of 2m digits goes from all zeros to all ones while the block gains 4m−1 words, for every n and every tape R right of it.

claims.title: What an overflow does
claims.text: Right of the counter lies junk (1110)^a T, T a second counter in the same digit code. When the main counter is all ones at even width w, the next two rounds leave it at width w+2 with value 2w+1 and take 1 and 2 words of 1110 in turn (three every two overflows), and every second overflow adds one to T. Simulated for small w and a (w ≤ 8, a from 6 to 9, 30 overflows in a row): the result does not depend on w or a. The overflows predicted this way fall on rounds 349,559, 8,738,167 and 25,515,383, one after the observed widenings of the visited region.

claims.title: Restarts
claims.text: When the 1110 words are used up the main counter absorbs the slow counter. If a leftover terminator remains, the next overflow restarts the machine: within three rounds the block (1011)^N becomes (1110)^N, the main counter of width W becomes the new slow counter 1111 1110 (1010)^(3W/4) 11 (or ... 1011 when W ≡ 2 mod 4) and a new, empty main counter starts. If nothing remains, the next overflow reads 0 in F and halts. From fresh epochs with a ≤ 40 words of junk and slow counters of widths 4, 6 and 8 (py/closure.py 40 4,6,8): 107 of the 120 runs restart in exactly this form (leftover 11), 6 restart with other leftovers and a variant tail (the second epoch's is 1111 1110 (1010)^(3W/4+1) 1011 1011), and 7 halt.

claims.title: Halting configurations exist in the family
claims.text: Starting from a fresh epoch (1110)^a plus the slow counter of width w, some junk lengths lead to a halt: for w = 6, a = 15, 18, 39, 42, 99, 102, 105, 108, 117, 120, 123, 126, ...; for w = 8, a = 51, 54, ..., 72, 87, 90, 147, 150, .... All are multiples of 3, in a Cantor-like pattern set by the digits of the slow counter. For the tail family left by the second epoch (... 1011 1011) no halts were found for widths 8, 12, 16 and a < 150.

claims.title: The second and third epochs end in restarts
claims.text: Skipping the 2k+2 overflows that only count the slow counter up (a shortcut checked against full runs at small sizes), the second epoch, junk 12,757,674 words, ends after its last overflows in a restart at counter width 17,010,256, with a block of N2 words, N2 a number of 17,010,257 bits (N2 ≡ 1 mod 3). The third epoch, junk N2, also ends in a restart: its last overflows absorb a slow counter of 17,010,257 digits and leave the terminator 11, simulated at the real width (17,010,270, then 17,010,272 counter digits). Extrapolated from small sizes, hence heuristic.

claims.title: Where the open question sits
claims.text: Each epoch's junk length is about the number of words the block grew in the epoch before, so the lengths grow like a tower: 12,757,674, then N<sub>2</sub> ≈ 2<sup>17,010,257</sup>, then a number of about (4/3)N<sub>2</sub> bits. The machine halts if and when an epoch's junk length falls in the halting set of its tail family, which is decided by residues and binary digits of these numbers. The fourth epoch needs the digits of a number of about 2<sup>17,010,257</sup> bits.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open. A proof of non-halting by a family of configurations closed under carry, overflow and restart is not possible as such: the family that the restarts produce contains halting members, so any such proof has to carry the exact arithmetic of the junk lengths from epoch to epoch. Not proved in Lean: the overflow round (the head sweeping into the junk, in two alignments), the slow counter's increment (symtm stops with NeedSplit on (11)^k), the absorption and the restart, and counters given as arbitrary bit lists rather than all zeros or all ones.

cd holdouts/1RB1LB_1RC0RD_0LA1RE_0RF1LC_1LA0RB_---1LC/py && python3 macro.py && python3 closure.py 40 4,6,8 && python3 shortcut.py
python3 epoch2.py && python3 epoch3.py && python3 ep3real.py   # epochs 2 and 3, a few minutes

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine builds a long block of identical words and, beside it, a binary counter that ticks once every two trips of the head. Each time the counter overflows it eats a little of the leftover cells beyond it; when they are gone, the whole block turns into new leftovers and everything starts again, each time on a vastly larger scale. Only at the end of such an epoch can the machine stop.

facts.text: Increments a counter of 2m digits makes from all zeros to all ones, proved in Lean for every m.
The first restart: the block of 12,757,674 words becomes the next epoch's leftovers. No halt before it.
About the leftover length of the fourth epoch; the second and third end in restarts.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 28,354 cells (20,782 left of the start, 11 right), with a density of 1s of 0.75.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A block of words, a counter, and leftovers
html: Everything happens left of the start. Write x for the word 1011. Each time the head reaches a new cell on the left in state B, the tape reads

The junction J is 1010 x and 11 x in turn. A round is one trip of the head from the left end into the counter and back. The block of x's grows by one word every two rounds, so the tape grows by two cells a round and a round costs time proportional to the tape length: the visited part grows like the square root of the time.

sections.heading: Crossing the block in one stroke
html: The head crosses the block of x's twelve steps a word on the way left (state A) and eight a word on the way right (state E), rewriting each word while it is on it and restoring it after. Lean proves the full bounce at the left end for every block length (left_turn, right_sweep). Because of this, the length of the block matters only for the time; the reduced simulator keeps it at 40 words and was checked against the full machine for 24,522 rounds; it is faithful until the first restart, where the real block becomes junk.

sections.heading: Overflows, epochs and restarts
html: Beyond the counter lies junk: a run of 1110 words and a second, slow counter. Each overflow of the main counter (the visited region widened at rounds 349,558, 8,738,166 and 25,515,382) takes one or two of the words, and every second overflow ticks the slow counter. When the words are gone the main counter swallows the slow one, and at the next overflow either the head reads 0 in state F, which halts, or the machine restarts: the whole block of 1011 words is rewritten as 1110 words, the counter becomes the new slow counter, and a new epoch begins with an empty counter.

The blank-tape run restarts at round 25,515,382 with 12,757,674 words of junk. An epoch with a words of junk lasts about 42a/3 rounds, and its block, the next epoch's junk, grows as large. Jumping from overflow to overflow, the second epoch ends in a restart with a junk of about 217,010,257 words, and so does the third. Halting starts exist (for some junk lengths divisible by 3, in a Cantor-like pattern), so whether the machine ever halts depends on the digits of these huge numbers.

family: binary counter beside a growing block
summary: A block of 1011 words grows at the left end while a binary counter next to it is incremented every two rounds and eats into junk at its far end; when the junk is gone the block becomes the next epoch's junk. Epochs 1 to 3 end in restarts; open.
